_comment: Tools the plugin's INSTALL.md names LITERALLY in a permissions ask rule. Claude Code ask rules do NOT accept wildcards, so these must be exact. If any is renamed or removed without updating INSTALL.md, the rule stops matching SILENTLY and the tool becomes blanket-allowed. Assert every name below still exists in the tool registry; fail the build if one does not.

tools.name: deploy_site
tools.why_gated: publishes a site to a real domain

tools.name: cms_schedule_set
tools.why_gated: schedules a content entry to publish at a set time, when Hiveku publishes the whole site

tools.name: deploy_run
tools.why_gated: runs a deploy

tools.name: deploy_serve_version
tools.why_gated: switches an environment to one of its earlier deployments: visitors get it within about a minute (a dry run is the default; the plugin's hook asks only on a start)

tools.name: deploy_build_cancel
tools.why_gated: stops a site's waiting and running builds (every build of the site unless build_type names one): the site keeps serving what it served before, so a change someone just published does not go live until it is deployed again

tools.name: project_publish_state_set
tools.why_gated: takes an environment of a site offline, unpublishes it (its server is deleted too, so coming back takes a full publish) or brings it back online: visitors stop reaching it, or reach it again, within minutes

tools.name: project_hosting_lane_set
tools.why_gated: chooses the hosting an environment that has never been published gets for its first publish

tools.name: project_hosting_lane_move
tools.why_gated: moves a published environment to other hosting, or undoes the move: undoing can show visitors errors for about a minute, and each custom domain then has to be pointed at the new target

tools.name: deploy_restore_files
tools.why_gated: puts a site's code files and images back as they were at a publish, as a new version on Your site, after a safety backup: code waits for the next publish, but an image stored at its live address changes on the live site without one

tools.name: project_domain_auto_configure
tools.why_gated: adds live DNS records for a domain whose DNS Hiveku runs: the domain starts pointing at this site, and what visitors reach there changes

tools.name: project_domain_transfer
tools.why_gated: moves a site's production domains and redirects to another site of the account: what the live address serves changes within minutes, and this site's own hiveku.com address can stop serving

tools.name: project_secrets_rename
tools.why_gated: renames a stored variable, or moves it between environments, sensitive ones too: code that reads the old name stops getting it

tools.name: site_convert_to_hosted
tools.why_gated: turns a site Hiveku only tracks into one Hiveku builds and hosts, from a new starter project, and it can never go back

tools.name: shopify_project_settings_set
tools.why_gated: saves which store Hiveku's own tools use for a website, or none: the live site does not change, but a running A/B test's purchase goal follows it at once

tools.name: webflow_connection_token_add
tools.why_gated: saves a Webflow site token as a connection. Without a project it becomes the account's default: a project that inherits the default with no site pinned moves to the site this token reaches, one pinned to a site the new token does not reach has no site until it is bound again, and one set to the current default directly, which every project made from one of its sites is, loses Webflow until it is bound again, even when the new token reaches its site. With a project on the Webflow CMS, the Content department and the AI write the newly bound site's collections. Form submissions from every site of a replaced default, and from a site this token takes over, stop reaching Hiveku and stay in Webflow until that site's webhooks are set up again

tools.name: webflow_project_site_bind
tools.why_gated: changes which Webflow site a project's tools, AI and Content department act on. Turning Webflow off, or leaving no site bound, switches its content source back to Hiveku's CMS

tools.name: webflow_connection_disconnect
tools.why_gated: disconnects a Webflow connection for every project that uses it: Hiveku's webhooks come off Webflow, and projects on the Webflow CMS switch back to Hiveku's CMS

tools.name: webflow_webhooks_reregister
tools.why_gated: re-registers Hiveku's webhooks on every site of a Webflow connection, for every project that uses it

tools.name: webflow_form_routing_set
tools.why_gated: changes which visitors' form submissions reach Hiveku: switched off, new ones stay in Webflow until they are imported

tools.name: webflow_form_submissions_backfill
tools.why_gated: copies past Webflow form submissions, with visitors' names, emails and answers, into Hiveku Forms and the CRM

tools.name: project_cookie_banner_set
tools.why_gated: changes what every visitor reads on the cookie banner from their next page load, with no deploy, Production included

tools.name: project_consent_trackers_add
tools.why_gated: adds a tracker that runs for visitors from their next page load, with no deploy; a custom snippet is code on the live site

tools.name: project_consent_trackers_update
tools.why_gated: changes a tracker visitors already get, from their next page load, with no deploy

tools.name: project_consent_trackers_remove
tools.why_gated: removes a tracker for good, and it stops on the live site from the next page load

tools.name: project_annotation_create
tools.why_gated: adds a comment to a site's review: it makes a task, tells the client's recipients and can start Auto-fix

tools.name: project_annotation_delete
tools.why_gated: deletes a review comment for good, and can take its task and that task's time logs with it

tools.name: project_annotation_comment_update
tools.why_gated: changes the words of a reply in a review comment's thread, which the client reads

tools.name: project_annotation_comment_delete
tools.why_gated: deletes a reply from a review comment's thread for good

tools.name: project_review_notify_set
tools.why_gated: changes where a client's review feedback goes: an email address or a Slack channel

tools.name: project_review_notify_test
tools.why_gated: sends a real test message to the email address or Slack channel named

tools.name: project_review_session_set
tools.why_gated: saves a login for this site's review frame: every guest of a review link gets that login and can read it

tools.name: project_review_session_clear
tools.why_gated: removes the site's saved reviewer login: reviewers lose it, and it cannot be read back

tools.name: project_files_bulk_save
tools.why_gated: overwrites project source

tools.name: project_vcs_commit
tools.why_gated: writes a commit

tools.name: project_vcs_merge
tools.why_gated: merges a branch

tools.name: project_vcs_pr_merge
tools.why_gated: merges a pull request (atomic branch merge)

tools.name: github_pr_merge
tools.why_gated: merges a pull request on the project's GitHub repository, and that push can deploy the site to every environment that follows the branch

tools.name: project_vcs_env_bind
tools.why_gated: changes which branch an environment deploys

tools.name: project_vcs_branch_delete
tools.why_gated: deletes a branch ref

tools.name: project_vcs_stash
tools.why_gated: moves pending work to a branch and resets the environment source (dry-run is the default, apply rewrites main/branch heads)

tools.name: project_vcs_prune
tools.why_gated: permanently destroys orphaned S3 tree bytes (dry_run defaults true; apply is unrecoverable)

tools.name: project_vcs_branch_preview_teardown
tools.why_gated: destroys a live branch preview app a client may be looking at - irreversible

tools.name: project_vcs_revert
tools.why_gated: moves a branch head back to an earlier commit and discards its uncommitted working-tree edits

tools.name: project_vcs_rollback
tools.why_gated: moves Your site or a branch back to an earlier version (saved as a new version; no deployed tier changes)

tools.name: project_vcs_restore_files
tools.why_gated: brings chosen files on Your site or a branch back as they were in an earlier version, and removes those that version did not have, saved as a new version (a dry run is the default; the plugin's hook asks only on an apply)

tools.name: project_vcs_resolve
tools.why_gated: settles merge conflicts on a branch by writing the chosen side, or the final text, of each conflicting file there and saving a version; that text replaces Your site's version when the review merges

tools.name: project_vcs_branch_in_step
tools.why_gated: records where a branch and Your site last matched, which changes what every later review into Your site counts as new

tools.name: project_vcs_pr_update
tools.why_gated: edits an open review: a new target branch changes where it merges and dismisses the approvals people gave, and marking a draft ready lets it merge

tools.name: project_vcs_queue_add
tools.why_gated: adds a review to its merge line, which then merges it into its target (into main: Your site) in the background with nobody asking again: joining the line is the approval to merge

tools.name: project_vcs_checks_rerun
tools.why_gated: runs a review's build and checks again, which spends the site's test builds (six per 15 minutes, shared with people and the merge line)

tools.name: project_secrets_set
tools.why_gated: writes a site's environment variables; a key without a tier reaches production, and the change is synced into the running site at once

tools.name: project_secrets_delete
tools.why_gated: removes a site's environment variable (with all: true, every one), and the running site loses it on its next sync or deploy

tools.name: project_secrets_apply_to_preview
tools.why_gated: copies the site's stored development values into the live preview, where code an AI writes runs, and restarts it

tools.name: project_secrets_reveal
tools.why_gated: hands the AI the plaintext values of a site's non-sensitive variables for one tier; a person also approves each reveal in the dashboard

tools.name: project_secrets_mark_sensitive
tools.why_gated: makes a site's stored variables write-only: their values are never shown again, to people or to AI tools, and only a person can make one readable again, with a new value

tools.name: project_secrets_replace
tools.why_gated: replaces one tier's environment variables with the set given: with apply it adds, changes and removes variables in one write, synced into the running site

tools.name: env_group_create
tools.why_gated: creates an account environment group, a set of variables that every site linked to it receives; it holds nothing and reaches no site until variables are set and a site is linked

tools.name: env_group_update
tools.why_gated: renames an account environment group or changes its description; people and agents pick groups by name, so a rename changes which group they link and edit

tools.name: env_group_delete
tools.why_gated: deletes an account environment group and every value in it, which cannot be restored; a group still linked to a site is refused

tools.name: env_group_set
tools.why_gated: writes or removes variables in an account environment group; every site linked to it gets the change in its running functions at once, and a name without a tier reaches production

tools.name: env_group_link
tools.why_gated: links an account environment group to a site: the group's variables join the site's environment in every tier, synced into its running functions at once, and the site's own variables still win

tools.name: env_group_unlink
tools.why_gated: unlinks an account environment group from a site: the site loses the group's variables in its running functions at once, which can break code that reads them

tools.name: project_ab_test_create
tools.why_gated: drafts a page A/B test; with make_copy it also commits a copy of the page to the site's code (saved as a version, not deployed)

tools.name: project_ab_test_update
tools.why_gated: changes a page A/B test; on a running test a new split moves the site's live visitors between the original and the second version

tools.name: project_ab_test_action
tools.why_gated: starts, pauses, resumes or ends a page A/B test on the live site, which decides the page real visitors get; ending on a winner also adds a redirect; after a test ends, promote or remove_copy saves a version on Main that changes the site's code, live after the next deploy

tools.name: project_ab_test_delete
tools.why_gated: deletes a page A/B test for good: a draft, or an ended test together with its results; a running or paused test must end first

tools.name: mobile_app_sdk_upgrade
tools.why_gated: moves a mobile app to a newer Expo SDK: rewrites its package files, app config and untouched template files in one go (a checkpoint is saved first) and restarts its preview

tools.name: mobile_app_identity_set
tools.why_gated: sets a mobile app's store identity (iOS bundle ID, Android package, link scheme); the IDs become permanent once a build is uploaded to a store

tools.name: mobile_app_apple_account_set
tools.why_gated: chooses which Apple developer account (store connection) a mobile app's builds and App Store submissions use; one shared by another account publishes the app from that account's Apple team

tools.name: mobile_app_expo_project_choose
tools.why_gated: chooses which Expo project a mobile app's builds and over-the-air updates go to, and sets its webhooks; when the app's store identity does not match that project, the next build makes a new store app

tools.name: project_checkpoint_restore
tools.why_gated: overwrites the project's files with a checkpoint's (and, with restore_database: true, replays the checkpoint's database copy into the live database)

tools.name: checkpoint_restore
tools.why_gated: overwrites the project's files with a checkpoint's (and, with restore_database: true, replays the checkpoint's database copy into the live database)

tools.name: history_restore_to_time
tools.why_gated: overwrites the project's files with their state at an earlier time; mode exact also removes every file added since (taken from the Hiveku app's own key only)

tools.name: project_backup_create
tools.why_gated: makes a new backup of a site: a full copy of its files, images and uploads and, when it has one, its database, kept until someone deletes it (the site does not change)

tools.name: checkpoint_delete
tools.why_gated: permanently deletes a checkpoint, a recovery point that cannot be recreated

tools.name: site_delete
tools.why_gated: destroys a site

tools.name: site_transfer
tools.why_gated: moves a website, with its leads, pages and content, to another workspace, where this workspace's people no longer reach it

tools.name: site_firewall_allow
tools.why_gated: adds an allowance at the edge firewall of a customer's site: the named client (a user-agent token on that site's hostnames, or an address everywhere on Hiveku hosting) skips the browser check from then on, and a careless token opens the site to any scraper that copies it

tools.name: site_firewall_trust_range
tools.why_gated: trusts one of a customer's own networks at the edge firewall: that address range then skips the per-address limit on the customer's site, so a wrong or too-wide range lets one network send the site unlimited counted requests

tools.name: site_firewall_remove
tools.why_gated: removes a firewall allowance and re-syncs the edge: the customer's monitor or audit tool is refused at the browser check again on its next request, which they see as a blank page, a 202, or a 403 with x-hiveku-firewall: blocked

tools.name: site_firewall_private_set
tools.why_gated: turns private mode on or off for one environment of a customer's site, or changes who it lets in: private can lock the customer's own people out, and public opens the environment to anyone with its address

tools.name: project_indexing_set
tools.why_gated: turns a site's search engine indexing on or off (Site > Hosting > Production): off tells Google and every other search engine to drop the live site from their results on every production address, custom domain included, and getting listed again can take weeks; on lets them list a site the owner may be keeping out of search on purpose

tools.name: project_concurrency_set
tools.why_gated: changes how many copies of a live site's server may run at once (Site > Hosting > Server capacity): a limit below its busy moments turns visitors' requests into error pages, and removing a limit lets a burst open more database connections than the site's database allows

tools.name: project_page_cache_set
tools.why_gated: switches page caching for a live site's Production (Site > Hosting > Page caching): on, the edge keeps the pages the site marks as shareable and hands them to visitors without reaching the server; off, every view reaches the server again

tools.name: project_cache_clear
tools.why_gated: clears what the CDN keeps for one deployed environment of a site: it costs money past the free allowance, spends the limit of 6 clears an hour per environment and 40 a day per account, and the next visitors to each path go to the site itself until the CDN holds its copies again

tools.name: project_cdn_invalidate
tools.why_gated: the same clear as project_cache_clear under its older name, on the same limits and at the same cost

tools.name: analytics_visitor_intelligence_start
tools.why_gated: starts identifying the people and companies who visit a live site (Site > Analytics > Visitor Intelligence): each one it finds counts against the account's monthly allowance, and stop_on_project_ids switches it off on the other sites named

tools.name: account_settings_update
tools.why_gated: changes shared account identity or timezone for everyone, affecting scheduling

tools.name: account_settings_logo_set
tools.why_gated: replaces the shared account logo for everyone

tools.name: account_settings_logo_remove
tools.why_gated: removes the shared account logo for everyone

tools.name: account_timezone_set
tools.why_gated: changes the account's timezone for everyone: scheduled posts and calendar days, report and dashboard day boundaries, and a phone receptionist with no zone of its own move with it; clearing it leaves each viewer's browser zone in charge

tools.name: account_memory_append
tools.why_gated: suggests a line for the account memory: until an owner reviews it on the dashboard, every department agent reads it at the start of each conversation (marked as not reviewed), so a wrong or planted line steers every department at once

tools.name: memory_update
tools.why_gated: replaces a department's whole memory document: a partial or stale copy silently erases everything else that department's agents read at the start of each conversation (History keeps the old version, but nobody sees it happen)

tools.name: memory_delete
tools.why_gated: deletes a memory entry: every agent that reads it stops seeing it at once (History keeps a copy to restore)

tools.name: memory_restore_version
tools.why_gated: puts an older version back over the current one: every change made since that version disappears from what the agents read

tools.name: memory_bulk_create
tools.why_gated: writes up to 100 memory entries in one call: a bad batch fills department memory with entries every agent reads

tools.name: account_memory_save
tools.why_gated: replaces the whole of About your business, the one document every agent reads: anything left out is gone from what every agent reads from their next conversation (history keeps the old text). Hiveku takes it from the Hiveku app's own key only

tools.name: account_memory_restore
tools.why_gated: puts an older version of About your business back over the current one: every agent reads the older text from their next conversation (the text it replaces stays in history). Hiveku takes it from the Hiveku app's own key only

tools.name: account_memory_suggest
tools.why_gated: files a line for About your business: it waits until an owner or admin keeps or removes it, and once kept every agent reads it. Hiveku takes it from the Hiveku app's own key only

tools.name: account_memory_suggestion_keep
tools.why_gated: adds a suggested line to About your business, which every agent reads from their next conversation. Hiveku takes it from the Hiveku app's own key only

tools.name: account_memory_suggestions_remove
tools.why_gated: removes suggested lines for About your business without keeping them. Hiveku takes it from the Hiveku app's own key only

tools.name: account_memory_suggestions_restore
tools.why_gated: puts removed suggestions for About your business back, to wait for an owner or admin again. Hiveku takes it from the Hiveku app's own key only

tools.name: agent_memory_save
tools.why_gated: replaces the whole text of one of an agent's rules, skills or notes: the agent follows the new text from its next conversation (history keeps the old version)

tools.name: agent_memory_remove
tools.why_gated: deletes one of an agent's rules, skills or notes: the agent stops following it straight away (it can be put back from Recently deleted in its history)

tools.name: agent_memory_create
tools.why_gated: adds a rule, skill, shortcut or specialist to an agent, which the agent follows from its next conversation

tools.name: agent_memory_restore
tools.why_gated: puts an older version of one of an agent's rules, skills or notes back over the current one: the agent follows the older text from its next conversation

tools.name: chief_of_staff_memory_save
tools.why_gated: replaces the whole text of one of the chief of staff's rules or notes, or adds a new one, which the chief of staff follows from the next conversation (history keeps the old version)

tools.name: chief_of_staff_memory_remove
tools.why_gated: deletes one of the chief of staff's rules or notes: the chief of staff stops following it straight away (a copy is kept under Recently deleted)

tools.name: website_memory_file_save
tools.why_gated: replaces the whole text of one of a website's memory files (CLAUDE.md and the rest), which the website agent follows from its next turn (history keeps the old version)

tools.name: website_memory_file_restore
tools.why_gated: puts an older version of a website's memory file back as the current one: the website agent follows the older text from its next turn

tools.name: agent_profile_save
tools.why_gated: changes an agent's profile: its name, picture, role, tone and instructions, which shape every conversation it has from the next one

tools.name: agent_switch_set
tools.why_gated: switches an agent on or off: switched off, it stops working for the account (Support hands its website chats to the team); switched on, it adds its starter rules and skills. Hiveku takes it from the Hiveku app's own key only

tools.name: voice_pronunciations_save
tools.why_gated: changes how the phone agents say names and words on every call, and how fast they speak: the list sent replaces the whole list

tools.name: marketplace_template_install
tools.why_gated: writes a Marketplace pack of rules and skills into an agent's memory (a website pack into one website's, or every website's), which the agent follows from its next conversation

tools.name: content_publish_to_site
tools.why_gated: publishes content publicly

tools.name: content_schedule
tools.why_gated: queues a public publish

tools.name: email_campaign_send_now
tools.why_gated: sends email to real recipients

tools.name: email_campaign_schedule
tools.why_gated: queues a real send

tools.name: email_campaign_resend_non_openers
tools.why_gated: re-sends to real recipients

tools.name: email_campaign_test_send
tools.why_gated: sends real mail to up to 5 addresses on the account's production SES lane

tools.name: workflow_email_step_test_send
tools.why_gated: sends real mail now on the account's own marketing domain lane, the same as email_campaign_test_send

tools.name: email_send
tools.why_gated: sends a real email through the account's Email Service as one of its API keys; with a production key it is delivered, and it cannot be taken back

tools.name: email_domain_send_instructions
tools.why_gated: emails a sending domain's DNS records to the person named, often someone outside the account, from Hiveku's platform address

tools.name: email_project_connect
tools.why_gated: makes a website's email keys and writes them, with its email settings, into the site's variables, which changes how the live site sends its email

tools.name: email_suppression_import
tools.why_gated: adds up to 5,000 addresses to the account's suppression list at once; imported bounces and complaints can never be removed, and nothing is emailed to them again

tools.name: email_webhook_delete
tools.why_gated: switches an email webhook off, and email_webhook_update can turn it back on; once Hiveku supports permanent: true, a call with it deletes the webhook for good with its delivery history, which cannot be brought back

tools.name: crm_envelope_send
tools.why_gated: sends a signature request

tools.name: crm_envelope_alerts_set
tools.why_gated: can add outside email addresses that get a contract's alerts and the client's signed contract, or turn its alerts off

tools.name: crm_contract_template_create
tools.why_gated: can add outside email addresses that get each client's signed contract for every contract started or bulk sent from the template

tools.name: crm_contract_template_update
tools.why_gated: can add outside email addresses that get each client's signed contract for every contract started or bulk sent from the template

tools.name: crm_envelope_create_from_template
tools.why_gated: can start a contract with outside email addresses, given or copied from its template, that get the client's signed contract

tools.name: crm_envelope_signer_reassign
tools.why_gated: changes who signs a sent contract and emails the new person a signing link

tools.name: crm_envelope_create
tools.why_gated: can start a contract with outside email addresses that get its alerts and the client's signed contract

tools.name: crm_envelope_update
tools.why_gated: can add outside email addresses that get a contract's alerts and the client's signed contract, or turn its alerts off

tools.name: crm_estimate_send
tools.why_gated: sends an estimate to a client

tools.name: helpdesk_ticket_send_reply
tools.why_gated: replies to a customer

tools.name: helpdesk_assistant_knowledge_sources_update
tools.why_gated: changes what the website assistant may tell anyone who opens the chat on the business's site: turning on its Google listing, website pages or documents, or sharing a knowledge base with it, lets visitors be told what those hold

tools.name: helpdesk_contact_data_erase
tools.why_gated: permanently erases one person's website chats, their files, chat visits, the CRM records kept for the chats and their own meeting recordings, with no undo; Hiveku refuses it through a key until the apps that ask first are out

tools.name: helpdesk_chat_retention_set
tools.why_gated: sets how long the account keeps website chats; every night, older chats are deleted for good with their messages and files; Hiveku refuses a real change through a key until the apps that ask first are out

tools.name: helpdesk_social_comments_settings_update
tools.why_gated: turns Facebook and Instagram comments into help desk tickets for chosen Pages: replies sent from those tickets post publicly under the person's comment, and alerts and response time targets start for every comment it lets in

tools.name: marketing_report_send
tools.why_gated: emails a report to a client

tools.name: ppc_budget_update
tools.why_gated: changes ad spend

tools.name: ppc_platform_budget_update
tools.why_gated: changes ad spend

tools.name: ppc_bid_modifier_update
tools.why_gated: changes ad spend

tools.name: ppc_keyword_bid_update
tools.why_gated: changes ad spend

tools.name: ppc_platform_keyword_bid_update
tools.why_gated: changes ad spend

tools.name: ppc_recent_change_override
tools.why_gated: turns a refused PPC change's override token into a person's yes: the same change sent again within 15 minutes goes over someone else's recent change to that budget, bid or setting, which the hold (7 days for budget and bidding, 24 hours for the rest) exists to protect

tools.name: ppc_bidding_strategy_update
tools.why_gated: changes how spend is allocated

tools.name: ppc_platform_bidding_strategy_update
tools.why_gated: changes how spend is allocated

tools.name: ppc_campaign_create
tools.why_gated: creates a spending campaign

tools.name: ppc_enable_resource
tools.why_gated: turns a paused Google Ads campaign, ad group, ad or keyword back on: it serves and spends from that moment, with no confirm step and no budget check on the call

tools.name: ppc_platform_enable_resource
tools.why_gated: turns a paused campaign, ad set, ad group or ad back on (Google, Microsoft, Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok, Amazon, Vibe or ChatGPT Ads): it serves and spends from that moment, with no confirm step and no budget check on the call

tools.name: ppc_bulk_edit
tools.why_gated: sets the status of up to 100 Google Ads campaigns, ad groups or keywords in one call, and any ENABLED operation starts spend at once; gated by name, so a pause-only call asks too (a single pause through ppc_pause_resource does not)

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_creatives
tools.why_gated: set-status enabled makes a LinkedIn ad deliverable at once when its campaign and group are active, and its confirm field is filled in by the agent, not a person; gated by name, so list and detail ask too

tools.name: ppc_tiktok_split_tests
tools.why_gated: create starts a TikTok split test that copies the campaigns or ad groups under test into cells and spends its budget from the start time, and update extends a running one; no confirm step; gated by name, so its reads ask too

tools.name: ppc_recommendation_apply
tools.why_gated: applies a Google Ads recommendation with Google's default settings for its type: it can change the bidding strategy, switch on broad match or search partners, or add keywords, so reach and spend change at once

tools.name: ppc_meta_campaign_update
tools.why_gated: a later stop_time puts a Meta campaign that has ended back into delivery, or keeps one spending past its stop date, and a new bid strategy changes what it pays; gated by name, so a rename asks too

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_campaign_update
tools.why_gated: a later end_date puts a LinkedIn campaign that has ended back into delivery, or keeps one spending past its end date, and archive ends it for good; gated by name, so a rename asks too

tools.name: ppc_linkedin_campaign_group_update
tools.why_gated: a later end_date puts a LinkedIn campaign group's campaigns back into delivery, a higher daily or total budget lets them spend more (group budgets are set nowhere else), and archive ends the group for good; gated by name, so a rename asks too

tools.name: ppc_google_auto_apply_set
tools.why_gated: enabling an auto-apply type lets Google apply its own recommendations (new keywords, broad match, search partners, CPA and ROAS targets) with nobody asking, so reach and spend change unattended
